comments4600.body:
## Cause upgraded from "sufficient mechanism" to **confirmed**, from committed data alone

The session that filed this work flagged — correctly — that nested-key drift was only proven *sufficient*, not proven to be what fired on 08-05: any body-mutating change (an `int→float` promotion, list-of-struct unification inside `spans`) yields the identical error shape. The real post-collect ledger was lost to a later `actions/checkout`, so the suggested confirmation route was to capture a runner artifact.

That turned out to be unnecessary. `validate_manifest_identity` computes `expected` from the body it just read, so the run's `expected` **is the drifted digest** — and it can be reproduced offline:

| candidate mutation applied to committed row 0 | resulting digest |
|---|---|
| **`file_number_provenance` + `collection_scope` → null** | **`bc364561bf32b58a…`** ← run 30960328285's `expected` |
| `file_number_provenance` alone | `6857c1ff0c2e557b…` |
| `collection_scope` alone | `0e4bf6d8377bb8e0…` |
| `byte_length` int→float | `ae0e757d7b9e3248…` |
| `document_version` int→float | `496b147e5965edb0…` |
| unmodified (control) | `42f684e8d81d58a3…` ← the run's `got` |

This **rules the alternates out** rather than merely offering a rival: any additional mutation would land on a different digest. So it is those two keys, exactly — the pair #4243 added at 08-01 23:44, after the last ledger commit at 18:11 — and no `spans` or dtype drift accompanied them.

Two corrections to my own PR body while I'm here:

- I wrote that the failure recurred deterministically. The filing session is right that this needed proof, and it has one: `_manifest_record` sets both keys **unconditionally**, and `_atomic_write` ran on every `fetch()`. An empty append is a plain round-trip, which I measured as 0/1258 failures — so a drifted ledger implies at least one row was appended, and any appended row necessarily carried both keys. Drift on append was guaranteed, not weather-dependent.
- The local-repro dead end was real and is worth recording: without `R2_*` the content-addressed store is unavailable, all document retrievals defer, and the append path never runs — so no lookback widening can reproduce it locally.

`tests/test_capital_structure_source_ledger_io.py::test_incident_hash_identifies_the_exact_pair_of_back_filled_keys` pins the above permanently. It is safe to pin because row 0 sits inside the immutable prefix.

**None of this changes the fix.** JSONL was chosen because it makes identity a function of the record alone, which removes the entire class — struct union, dtype promotion, and `spans` unification alike — since a JSON line has no cross-row schema to unify and no type inference on read. The diagnosis being narrower than the fix is the right way round.
